svg.title: Three things kill a script. Each has exactly one defence.
svg.desc: A backup.sh box in the centre attacked from three sides: an unquoted variable that word-splits into two tokens, two scheduled copies starting at the same time, and a SIGTERM arriving mid-write. Beside each attack the fix is drawn in green — quoting the variable, an atomic mkdir lock, and write-to-temp-then-rename. Below, a crossed-out trap for SIGKILL and a three-run idempotence checklist where runs two and three must change nothing.
svg.text: Three things kill a script. Each has exactly one defence.
out.txt is now half a file
rename() is atomic on one filesystem
if run 2 does work, it is not idempotent - just lucky
mkdir is ATOMIC. test-then-create is a race with a
window you will never see in testing.
...at what point does this stop being
